memory.peak_rss_scope: macOS process cumulative high-water mark, not isolated method allocation

limitations: No MCFOST execution or real RT products used
No FITS decompression, I/O, hashing, all-component checks, or quality-check scans timed
No claim of full historic kernel equivalence; same one-plane aperture/PSF numerical operation compared
Cold path still performs one full-frame Gaussian convolution of aperture weights; warm benefit requires matching geometry and PSF within one process
Four-entry LRU may evict weights in longer wavelength cycles; new process starts cold
New reader still loads and finite-checks all eight input planes once; only subsequent calculations use plane zero
Repeated separated-component convolutions and repeated file hashing in historical workflow are not included in timing baseline
64 subpixels chosen for exact convention parity; runtime default is 16, not a convergence-equivalent claim

retained: Signed total-I aperture and total-flux positivity; all input planes finite and expected total-I/component header labels
Angular WCS, square pixel, centred CRPIX, wavelength, units, and aperture plus six-sigma PSF support
Plane-0 positive border-flux fraction below 1e-3 and signed full-field convolution loss below 1e-4
Optional plane-0 coeval SED closure at absolute relative difference <=1e-5, without renormalization
Negative-flux fraction and adjoint zero-clipping sensitivity recorded as diagnostics, not scoring substitutions
intentionally_omitted: Full separated-component significance, closure, active-morphology, aperture-fraction, and intrinsic integrity gates
Historical per-pixel Python math.fsum accumulation; new float64 NumPy summation is tested on synthetic rather than all archived realizations
Repeated full input-file hashing and frozen task-identity validation inside measurement; runner handles execution provenance
Explicit multi-seed, pixel-scale, temperature, and convergence validation
lightweight_validation_review.distinction: Passing these lightweight checks is not the same claim as passing the full historical measurement contract.
